name: The Black Iron Prison Vision
summary: PKD reports a recurring vision in which 1974 California is overlaid by 70 AD Rome — a vast iron prison housing the early Christians under imperial persecution. The vision continued at intervals through 1981.
description: Beginning in 1974 and recurring throughout the Exegesis years, PKD reports a vision in which late-twentieth-century California is overlaid by first-century Rome — specifically Rome around 70 AD, after the destruction of the Temple, when the early Christians were a persecuted minority under the empire. He calls this the Black Iron Prison. The Nixon administration is read as the empire; the FBI as the Roman secret police; PKD himself as the apostle Thomas in hiding. The vision provides the central frame for *VALIS*, *The Divine Invasion*, and *Radio Free Albemuth*.

pkd_interpretations.interpretation: Time is dysphasic — the apparent linear flow is illusion; we are simultaneously in 70 AD and 1974.
The Black Iron Prison is the gnostic counterfeit world produced by the demiurge to imprison souls.
The Black Iron Prison is the structural metaphor underlying all my fiction since *Time Out of Joint* (1959).

scholar_interpretations.interpretation: McKee identifies the Black Iron Prison as the gnostic-Christian core of PKD's late theology.
Davis frames the BIP as PKD's distinctive contribution to American gnostic-conspiracy thought.
Jameson reads the BIP/Empire-overlay as PKD's allegorical mode for late capitalism.

primary_sources.excerpt: Hundreds of segments invoke the Black Iron Prison.
*VALIS* (1981) is structured around the BIP/Empire overlay.

contradiction_zone: no — universally treated as PKD's central metaphor
